mainTopic: The opening of פרק אלו נערות: which young women receive the קנס, and the dispute between רבי מאיר and חכמים about the קנס for a קטנה
overview: The third פרק of כתובות opens with a משנה listing young women whose rapist must pay the קנס even though they have flawed lineage, such as a ממזרת, a נתינה and a כותית. It adds converts, captives and maidservants whose new status began before age three years and one day. It also adds forbidden relatives and a נדה, because those sins carry כרת and not מיתת בית דין. The גמרא asks whether the list means girls with proper lineage get no קנס. It answers that the list only adds the flawed cases. The גמרא then notes that the משנה speaks of a נערה and not a קטנה, and רב identifies this with רבי מאיר. A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר holds a קטנה can be sold but gets no קנס, and a נערה gets the קנס but cannot be sold. חכמים give the קנס from age three years and one day. The גמרא asks whether חכמים deny the father's right of sale, and it begins to correct their wording, a correction that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Young women with flawed lineage still receive the fine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists women of flawed lineage, and former captives, converts and maidservants, whose rapist must pay the קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the young women for whom a fine is paid: a ממזרת, a נתינה, and a כותית. The fine is also paid for a convert, a captive, and a maidservant, as long as they were ransomed, converted, or freed before age three years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens with a list of young women whose rapist must pay the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group (ממזרת, נתינה, כותית) are Jewish women whose lineage is flawed, yet they still get the קנס. The second group (גיורת, שבויה, שפחה) qualify only if their new status began before three years and one day, so they still count as a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The fixed fine of fifty shekels a rapist pays the girl's father
A young woman, roughly from twelve until six months later
A girl born from a forbidden union
A Gibeonite woman
A Samaritan woman
A woman taken captive

phrases.english: These are the young women for whom there is a fine:
One who has relations with a mamzeret
or with a Gibeonite woman, or with a Samaritan woman;
one who has relations with a convert, or with a captive woman,
or with a maidservant
who were ransomed, or converted, or were freed,

phrases.aramaic: פְּחוּתוֹת מִבְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: when they were less than three years and one day old.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קנס is paid for a ממזרת, נתינה, and כותית, and for a convert, captive, or maidservant whose change of status came before age three years and one day.

steps.title: Forbidden relatives still receive the fine when there is only כרת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists forbidden relatives and a נדה whose rapist pays the קנס, because these sins carry כרת and not מיתת בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with his sister, his father's sister, his mother's sister, his wife's sister, his brother's wife, his father's brother's wife, or a נדה must pay the fine. Even though these carry כרת, there is no death penalty from בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list with women who are forbidden to the man, and says he still pays the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key reason is at the end: these sins are punished by כרת from Heaven, not by a court execution. The משנה implies that if בית דין would execute him, he would not pay the קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual state
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven
A death penalty carried out by the court
Even though

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the principle that a court death penalty cancels a money payment for the same act, while a heavenly punishment like כרת does not.

phrases.english: One who has relations with his sister,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו, וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: or with his father's sister, or with his mother's sister,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִשְׁתּוֹ, וְעַל אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו,
phrases.english: or with his wife's sister, or with his brother's wife,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אָבִיו, וְעַל הַנִּדָּה
phrases.english: or with his father's brother's wife, or with a menstruating woman
there is a fine for them.
Even though they are punished with karet,
there is no court-imposed death penalty for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with forbidden relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קנס is paid even for forbidden relatives and a נדה, since these carry כרת and not מיתת בית דין.

steps.title: Do only flawed young women get the fine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording, which sounds like only flawed women receive the קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: These young women: do the flawed ones get a fine, and the proper ones do not?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the opening words of the משנה, since "these are the young women" sounds like a complete list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is the full list of who gets a קנס, it would mean a girl with proper lineage gets nothing. That cannot be right, since the תורה's קנס is clearly about an ordinary Jewish girl.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion explaining the משנה
Women with flawed lineage
Women with proper lineage
They have

phrases.english: GEMARA: These young women,
flawed ones have a fine,
but proper ones do not?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי נְעָרוֹת, פְּסוּלוֹת אִית לְהוּ קְנָס, כְּשֵׁירוֹת לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the opening wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's opening phrase אלו נערות שיש להן קנס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the list as complete would wrongly exclude girls with proper lineage from the קנס.

steps.title: The list adds flawed women to the fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה means: these are the flawed young women who still receive the קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: these are the flawed young women who also have a fine: a ממזרת, a נתינה, and a כותית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה as listing only the surprising cases of flawed women who still get the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper girl obviously gets the קנס, so the משנה did not need to mention her. The list exists to teach that even flawed lineage does not cancel the קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying proper girls lack the קנס. It is saying the משנה only bothered to list the flawed cases, because those are the new teaching.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ נְעָרוֹת פְּסוּלוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם קְנָס
phrases.english: These are the flawed young women for whom there is a fine:
One who has relations with a mamzeret
or with a Gibeonite woman, or with a Samaritan woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading the משנה's opening phrase.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: adding the word פסולות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists the only girls who receive the קנס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists the flawed girls who receive the קנס in addition to proper girls.
steps.whatToRemember: The list in the משנה adds flawed girls to the קנס; it does not take it away from proper girls.

steps.title: Which תנא excludes a minor from the fine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה speaks of a נערה and not a קטנה, and asks which תנא holds that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: A young woman, yes; a minor, no. Who is the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the word נערות and asks whose opinion it matches. This sets up a search for the source in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה says נערות, it implies a קטנה (under twelve) gets no קנס. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this, since not all agree.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl under twelve
Yes
Who is the author of this teaching?

phrases.english: A young woman, yes; a minor, no.
Who is the tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲרָה אִין, קְטַנָּה לָא. מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new inference from the משנה's word נערות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the קנס applies to a נערה but not to a קטנה.

steps.title: The answer: the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says the משנה that gives the קנס only to a נערה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: this משנה is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. The משנה that speaks only about a נערה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 noticed that the משנה gives the קנס to a נערה and says nothing about a קטנה. רב says this fits רבי מאיר, who holds that a קטנה gets no קנס at all. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is', here meaning 'this משנה follows the view of...'

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: He means that the משנה we are learning follows רבי מאיר's opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 5 about which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a קטנה does not receive the קנס.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר holds a קטנה can be sold but gets no קנס, and a נערה gets the קנס but cannot be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a girl from one day old until she grows two hairs can be sold by her father, but gets no קנס. From when she grows two hairs until she becomes a בוגרת, she gets the קנס but cannot be sold. These are the words of רבי מאיר, who used to say: wherever there is sale there is no קנס, and wherever there is קנס there is no sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי מאיר really gives the קנס only to a נערה. This proves that our משנה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר splits a girl's life into two stages. As a קטנה, before two hairs, her father can sell her as an אמה עבריה, but she gets no קנס. As a נערה, from two hairs until she becomes a בוגרת, she gets the קנס but can no longer be sold. His rule is that sale and קנס never go together, so the משנה's focus on the נערה fits him exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Sale: a father's right to sell his young daughter as a maidservant
Two hairs: the sign of physical maturity that turns a קטנה into a נערה
Until she becomes a בוגרת, a fully grown woman
The fixed fine paid by a rapist or seducer

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a קטנה can be sold but gets no קנס; a נערה gets the קנס but cannot be sold. Sale and קנס never overlap.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Sale' here does not mean selling her for marriage. It means the father's right to sell his young daughter as an אמה עבריה, a Jewish maidservant.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A minor girl, from one day old
until she grows two hairs —

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ מֶכֶר וְאֵין לָהּ קְנָס.
phrases.english: there is sale for her, and there is no fine for her.
phrases.notes: 'Sale' means her father may sell her as a Jewish maidservant.

phrases.english: And from when she grows two hairs until she becomes fully grown —

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ קְנָס וְאֵין לָהּ מֶכֶר.
phrases.english: there is a fine for her, and there is no sale for her.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
For Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֶכֶר — אֵין קְנָס,
phrases.english: Any place where there is sale — there is no fine,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קְנָס — אֵין מֶכֶר.
phrases.english: and any place where there is a fine — there is no sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs up רב's claim in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי מאיר's rule that sale and קנס never overlap, so only a נערה receives the קנס.

steps.title: חכמים give the קנס even to a young girl
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, חכמים say a girl from three years and one day old until she is fully grown receives the קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: a girl from three years and one day old until she becomes fully grown receives the קנס.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opinion of חכמים, who disagree with רבי מאיר. For them, even a קטנה from age three receives the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים start the קנס at three years and one day, well before the two hairs. So for them the קנס is not limited to a נערה, and our משנה cannot follow them. Their words also seem to say nothing about sale, which the גמרא questions next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages: the majority view disagreeing with רבי מאיר
Three years and one day: the age when, for חכמים, the קנס begins

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: קְטַנָּה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: A minor girl, from three years and one day old
until she becomes fully grown — there is a fine for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא, showing why the משנה cannot follow חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, a girl from three years and one day until she is fully grown receives the קנס, including a קטנה.

steps.title: Do חכמים really mean a young girl cannot be sold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: חכמים mention only the קנס. Do they mean that a קטנה cannot be sold?
steps.simpleTranslation: A fine, yes; but sale, no?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of חכמים. They mentioned only the קנס, which makes it sound as if they deny the father's right to sell a קטנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר listed both things, sale and קנס, for each stage. חכמים list only the קנס, so it sounds as if they hold there is no sale. That cannot be right, since a father may sell his young daughter, so their words need fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No

phrases.english: A fine, yes — but sale, no?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is surprised: a father can surely sell his young daughter, so חכמים can't mean there is no sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the חכמים's statement quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of חכמים in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By listing only the קנס, חכמים seem to deny the father's right of sale, which cannot be correct.

steps.title: The גמרא begins to correct the wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to give a corrected reading of the חכמים's words.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to tell us how to reread the words of חכמים, and the corrected wording comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אימא' means the original wording was not exact and should be read differently. The fix will answer the problem from step 9 and make sure חכמים do not deny the father's right of sale.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say': it signals a corrected reading of a text

phrases.english: Say:
phrases.notes: The corrected wording of חכמים comes in the next line of the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the question in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חכמים seemed to hold that a קטנה can receive the קנס but cannot be sold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The corrected wording comes in the next line; it will show that חכמים do not deny the right of sale.
